correctness.rationale: The 16-dimensional cubic quotient is exhausted by masks1..65535, 683 S5 orbits; an ideal-unit Gröbner test on 3 covering Q charts is equivalent to geometric smoothness, yielding 254 smooth orbits (27060 sections). Exact binary sextic and conjugate-line GF4 tests are equivalent to distinct degree-3 double contacts. Direct checks of all 27060 smooth coefficient masks reproduce the joint spectrum, total counts (10300,12810,3600,350) and six extremal orbits; an alternate SymPy ideal computation agreed.

originality.rationale: Xarles fully classifies abstract genus-four curves and supplies finite-field equations and point counts, but the inspected paper and public Magma code/data do not tabulate the proper rational tritangent spectrum by nonsplit quadric plane type. Kulkarni et al work over the reals; Bergström–Faber–Payne treat moduli counts and marked points, not contact multiplicities. Related known classifications concern split quadrics or genus-one nonsplit sections. Direct claim-implication comparisons give no covering statement. Priority risk is acknowledged because another computation might yield the same data.

value.rationale: The incidence of rational tritangent planes is a classical canonical curve invariant. For the nonsplit quadric its 10 smooth-conic rational planes and 5 quadric-tangent rational planes have distinct contact geometry; their 33 joint point/contact strata and six extremal projective types are mathematically motivated and not a renaming of the abstract genus-four point census. The precise five-rational-point obstruction and both kinds of maximal contact configurations are meaningful boundaries.
